title: DATEDIF vs YEARFRAC: whole units or a fraction
meta_desc: DATEDIF vs YEARFRAC: completed years/months/days versus decimal years with day-count conventions. Which one for ages, tenure, and accruals.
intro: Both measure the distance between two dates in year-terms, but they answer different questions: DATEDIF counts COMPLETED calendar units (a person is 34 until their birthday), YEARFRAC returns a DECIMAL (34.53 years) under a chosen day-count convention. Ages want the first; accruals and prorating want the second.

cols: Whole completed years / months / days (by unit code)
34.9972 the day before; needs INT() and care
Undocumented in Excel's wizard (Lotus legacy) but fully working
Universal — verified despite the missing docs

when.use_when: Human-calendar answers: ages, tenure as '34 years, 5 months' (Y + YM), countdown displays. Avoid the "MD" unit for month-end edge cases — it has documented quirks in Excel itself.
Money math over time: interest accruals, prorated fees, service-fraction calculations — choosing the basis deliberately (1 for real calendars, 0/30-360 only when a contract says so).

compat_note: Both execute identically in every LibreOffice version we test (desktop Excel behavior per docs — we do not run desktop Excel; Google Sheets is executed separately, see each function page) — DATEDIF works fine everywhere despite Excel never listing it in the function wizard, and YEARFRAC's basis codes agree cross-app (verified: basis 0 gives exactly 0.5 for Jan 1 → Jul 1; basis 1 gives 0.4959). Excel for the web is a separate application with its own calculation engine, and that one we do execute: all 11 corpus cases for these functions matched the documented values there (recalculated on OneDrive, 2026-09-01); the per-case values are on the individual function pages.
